findings.basis: Key read, no candidate value. Android default is empty. Google CarrierSettings carries the key in about 3300 kodiak textprotos, pointing either at com.android.imsserviceentitlement/.WfcActivationActivity or at com.google.android.wfcactivation activities (WfcActivationActivity, VzwEmergencyAddressActivity, WfcActivationCanadaActivity, DishWfcActivationActivity); the latter are not installed on LineageOS, so the served value's basis depends on which app it names and whether that app exists on the device.
findings.effect: The key names the activity that must approve Wi-Fi calling (WFC) before it is turned on, not only a screen. Settings: when the user turns the WFC switch on, after the disclaimer Settings launches the named component with LAUNCH_APP_ACTIVATE and calls setVoWiFiSettingEnabled(true) only on RESULT_OK; with the key empty it turns WFC on directly (WifiCallingSettingsForSub.java:565-588). getCarrierActivityIntent builds the intent from the string without checking the component exists (509-531), and the launch is not guarded, so a component that is not installed leaves the user unable to turn WFC on from Settings. The same value shows the 'Update emergency address' entry (186-196, 600-620). The Wi-Fi calling slice/quick toggle refuses to turn WFC on at all when the key is set, only off (WifiCallingSliceHelper.java:367-399, 525-555). The target apps on this ROM can also turn WFC off: ImsServiceEntitlement's activation and address-update flows return RESULT_OK only after a TS.43 entitlement check and call turnOffWfc when the server reports incompatible or missing data (WfcActivationController.java:285-310, 355-380); QNS's WfcActivationHelper enables WFC itself (225). QNS keys and CarrierConfigManager.ImsServiceEntitlement keys are documented as effective only when this key points to that app (WfcCarrierConfigManager.java:42-90; CarrierConfigManager.java:5020-5035, 5088-5100). The key is not read by Telephony, the AOSP ImsStack or the OCD ImsStack fork. Both com.android.imsserviceentitlement and com.android.telephony.qns are installed on the phone (24.0); Google's com.google.android.wfcactivation is not part of LineageOS.
findings.risk: The value decides whether and how Wi-Fi calling can be enabled and whether the carrier's emergency (dispatchable) address is collected first. A value naming a missing app blocks enabling WFC (Settings launch fails, slice cannot enable), so no emergency call can be carried over Wi-Fi where there is no cellular coverage; an entitlement-app value can switch WFC off on a server answer; an empty value enables WFC without registering an emergency address, so on carriers that route Wi-Fi emergency calls by the registered address the PSAP routing and location for such a call may be missing or wrong.

notes: Hold: the key stays in group A. It is not display only: it gates turning Wi-Fi calling on (Settings requires the named app's approval, the slice cannot turn it on), it points at apps that can turn Wi-Fi calling off after an entitlement check, and it decides whether the carrier's emergency address for Wi-Fi emergency calls is registered. Those change whether and how an emergency call can be placed and routed over Wi-Fi.
